newsitem.title: USA: Avitar sets job cuts, cash control measures.
newsitem.headline: Avitar sets job cuts, cash control measures.

text.p: Avitar Inc, a healthcare products maker, said Friday that, because of reduced revenues, it has adopted cash-control measures, including select hourly and salaried staff reductions and paying certain employees equity instead of cash.

Peter Phildius, chairman and chief executive officer, said that, at the same time, Avitar is investing in marketing and product development to increase its ability to seize business opportunities as they arise.

He expects current efforts to expand the company's customer base for wound dressing and urine-based rapid diagnostic test products. This would establish a strong base for the distribution of the company's saliva-based diagnostic tests as those products are brought to the market, he said.
"As revenues increase, we anticipate that Avitar's cash flow wil break even by the end of fiscal 1997 and that we will achieve profitability in fiscal 1998," he said.

For the second quarter ended March 31, the company said it posted a net loss of $1.004 million, or $0.10 a share, on revenues of $463,000. This compares with a net loss of $398,000, or $0.08 a share, on revenues of $1.226 million for the quarter a year ago, it said.
